analysis: Diabetes insipidus is characterized by a deficiency in antidiuretic hormone (ADH) or a renal insensitivity to it, leading to the production of large volumes of dilute urine. This results in a low urine osmolality because the kidneys are unable to concentrate the urine effectively. Standard medical knowledge indicates that urine osmolality in Diabetes insipidus is typically less than 300 mmol/L. This aligns with the enhanced information provided, which supports the consensus that the urine osmolality is <300 mmol/L in this condition.
